title: Console consumption requests intake & prioritization framework
creator: Aisha Raman
description:
Problem: Over the last 6 months we have seen a growing number of enterprise customers and platform teams asking for bespoke and self-serve console/reporting features: scheduled CSV/BigQuery exports, per-team and per-route cost breakdowns, long-term retention of usage snapshots for audits, and richer ad-hoc analytics. Requests are coming from Sales, Support, and Solution Engineering in inconsistent formats which leads to long scoping cycles and missed SLAs.

Goal: Create a repeatable intake + prioritization framework for console/reporting requests that: 1) reduces time-to-response for enterprise asks to <=3 business days for initial scope; 2) produces a prioritized backlog with clear acceptance criteria & compliance checks; 3) identifies reusable components (export templates, aggregation pipelines, RBAC filters) to minimize bespoke work; 4) produces a pilot deliverable (scheduled exports & a per-tenant cost breakdown card) for Q2.

Scope (non-bug): This ticket covers intake, triage rubric, prioritization matrix, stakeholder communications, and scoping of a 1st pilot. Actual engineering epics for pipeline/export/dashboard work will be created as children once triaged.

Out-of-scope: implementing export pipelines, infra-level billing exports for external accounting systems (unless scoped as a pilot), UI polishing beyond an initial console card and CSV download prototype.
acceptance_criteria: A clear intake form (Zendesk + product request form) and triage playbook are published and linked from the Console customer support page.
Prioritization rubric documented and used to score at least 12 outstanding requests; scores and resulting backlog order saved in Console Analytics project board.
At least one engineering epic (ENG-) and one design ticket (DES-) created for the pilot: scheduled CSV export and per-tenant cost breakdown card, with initial estimates and owners.
Security & privacy checklist completed for export data shape and retention; legal reviewed for customer data attachments.
Stakeholders (Sales, Solutions, Support) notified of the new intake SLA and escalation path.
Pilot scope agreed and scheduled into cycle 2026-W12 or earlier with documented success metrics (e.g., export latency, completeness, number of customers onboarded).
Acceptance criteria and scoring results added to this ticket and to the Console Analytics Confluence page.
proposed_flow: 1) Intake: customer asks via Support ticket or Solutions request -> submit to canonical product request form (linked).
2) Triage (within 3 business days): PM reviews submission, classifies into categories: Self-serve, Enterprise export, Regulatory/audit, or Partner integration.
3) Security/Privacy Check (if export includes PII/customer identifiers): Security kick-off within 5 business days; put 'blocker' flag on heavy compliance items.
4) Prioritize using rubric -> assign priority & expected runway (Pilot/Small work/Custom).
5) Create project artifacts: Epic (ENG-), Design ticket (DES-), and link to request. Provide initial estimate and target release window.
6) Customer communication: automated acknowledgement, PM assigned, estimated timeline & possible workarounds (e.g., manual exports while building).
7) Monitor: add to Console Analytics board; review weekly with Engineering leads for capacity alignment.
prioritization_matrix: Scoring dimensions (example weights): Revenue at risk / ARR exposure (30%), Compliance / SLA requirement (25%), Number of customers impacted (20%), Reusability / platform leverage (15%), Implementation complexity (10% - inverse scoring).
Tie-breakers: highest revenue, then compliance needs, then quick wins that unlock self-serve capabilities.
notes: Trade-offs: build generic export pipeline vs deliver targeted per-customer CSVs. Recommend: prioritize generic components (templated exports, RBAC filters) and allow bespoke attachments for largest customers in short-term.
Performance: frequent large exports can increase runtime cost and affect SLOs. Engineering to evaluate throttling, async job queues, and snapshotting approaches as part of epic scoping.
Data fidelity: cost attribution requires aligning token-level billing model with route/mapping metadata — may require small schema changes in telemetry stamps.
Compliance: scheduled exports to external storage (S3/GCS) require KMS/HSM key policies and audit trails. Security must own retention & delete policies for pilot.
Customer success/handoff: Solutions Engineering will provide 2 pilot customers and own onboarding playbook for the pilot phase.
